categories.title: Servers
categories.description: Serving requests and running work: the HTTP framework and its request and response values, WebSockets, DNS and MQTT brokers, job queues and schedules, and the base for building servers.

categories.title: Transport
categories.description: Reaching other services: HTTP and SMTP clients, NATS, and connection strings.

categories.title: Data
categories.description: Keeping data: databases and the queries over them, caches and file storage.

categories.title: Security
categories.description: Who is calling and how often: password hashing, sessions, tokens, OAuth2 and passkeys, and abuse limits.

categories.title: Observability
categories.description: Seeing what a service does: audit trails, telemetry, tracing spans and usage metrics.

categories.title: Platform
categories.description: The ground a service runs on: CLIs and consoles, configuration, dependency injection and registries, system information, locks, pools, circuit breakers, events, and the PHP engine semantics the Rust crates share.

categories.title: Utilities
categories.description: Focused helpers: input validation, translations, domain and email parsing, user-agent and device detection, OpenAPI documents, compression, load balancing and image processing.

categories.title: Integrations
categories.description: Third-party services: AI agents, version control, orchestration, CDNs, messaging providers for email, SMS and push, and moving data between backends.
